item.title: They said it couldn’t be done
item.description: The first ever Mini Globe Race sails into the history books as finishers arrive in Antigua having covered 24,000 miles solo around the globe in the past 13 months. Racing 19-foot Globe 580 yachts, 13 men and two women took part in the multi-stage competition. Renaud Stitelmann (SUI) won every leg and set a benchmark time of 180 days 11 hours 25 minutes and 57 seconds. item.title: Bacardi Cup: Cayard ends 45-year pursuit
item.description: After 45 years of chasing one of sailing’s most storied trophies, Paul Cayard (USA) finally won the Star Class Bacardi Cup in Miami, FL. The 2026 event on March 2-7 was the 99th edition, and Cayard and his crew Frithjof Kleen put the cherry on top of their legendary year: after winning the 2025 Star World Championship, Cayard now claims the coveted title. “A dogfight for the ages” — The trophy was hard-earned. item.description: A spirited rally by Cal Poly Maritime and relentless assault by the remainder of the fleet threatened – but couldn’t topple – College of Charleston as they held on to win the 2026 Port of Los Angeles Harbor Cup held on March 6-8 in Los Angeles, CA. item.description: With ‘Give to Gain’ as the theme for 2026's International Women's Day (March 8), World Sailing provided the stories of six volunteers from The Magenta Project who offered their time to create more opportunities for women in the sport. item.title: Taking positive steps for women
item.description: Improving participation for women at the highest end of the sport has required regulation. The Ocean Race 2017-18 (formerly Volvo Ocean Race) introduced a rule incentivizing mixed crews to improve gender diversity, with the 2023 edition requiring all teams to include at least one woman in the crew. The SailGP league did the same mid-way through Season 2 in October 2021. When Sailing at the Paris 2024 Olympics had equal participation and medal events for men and women, it was by design. item.title: Who are Chris Draper and Seb Menzies?
item.description: For Team New Zealand to defend the America's Cup in 2027, they will need to do it without 3-time winning skipper Peter Burling. With the keys handed to his 2024 co-helm Nathan Outteridge, the question then was who would be on the wheel across the boat. The newly appointed skipper has let it be known that Chris Draper and Seb Menzies will be getting that opportunity as the team begins training in their AC75 on the Hauraki Gulf, Auckland. For some background on the candidates, click here.

item.title: Same hull, New configuration for 2027
item.description: There were 11 crew when the AC75 was first introduced for the 36th America’s Cup, with the crew reduced to eight for the next edition and now five sailors for the racing in 2027. With the hulls being reused from 2024, modifications are needed to adapt to the new crew limit. The first look has come as Team New Zealand has relaunched their AC75 Taihoro at the Wynyard Point base in Auckland.
